talks.title: 0x10: David El - Behind the Cheats: A Tale About the Greedy Cheat Developer
talks.teaser: Examines 0x10: David El - Behind the Cheats: A Tale About the Greedy Cheat Developer and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: David El of CyberArk presents at SEC-T on the intersection of malware research and game cheat development, culminating in a case study of a greedy cheat developer caught red-handed.

Key Topics: Evolution of game cheats from memory editing to sophisticated anti-detection; Cheat Engine's core memory-scanning functionality; how game developers evolved protections; and forensic investigation of cheat developer operations.

Technical Details: El explains Cheat Engine's value correlation technique—scanning memory for on-screen values, changing them, and re-scanning to locate game variables. He traces how anti-cheat systems detect memory manipulation and how cheat developers monetize their tools.

Takeaways: Game cheat ecosystems share malware development techniques and criminal infrastructure. Security researchers can apply malware analysis skills to understand and disrupt cheat developer operations.

talks.title: 0x10: Anton Sapozhnikov & Samuel Kelemen - Path to an Advanced Vulnerability Management...
talks.teaser: Details 0x10: Anton Sapozhnikov & Samuel Kelemen - Path to an Advanced Vulnerability Management and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Einride Context

Anton Sapozhnikov and Samuel Kelemen describe building vulnerability management at Einride, an electric freight and charging company operating cloud services, office IT, autonomous trucks, and IoT charging stations across diverse environments.

Unified Data Plane

They aggregate roughly 60,000 findings from Orca Security (cloud/containers), Dependabot, Semgrep (code), and CrowdStrike Falcon (devices) into a central BigQuery security data lake rather than forcing developers across 22 teams to use separate panes of glass.

Metrics and Reporting

The program tracks vulnerability counts by source and type, SLA compliance, and evolution over time. Slack messages correlate categories with originating scanners so teams see consistent status across laptops, cloud, vehicles, and charging infrastructure.

Ongoing Challenges

Speakers discuss disagreements on severity, non-applicable findings with mitigating controls, and unsolved scaling problems. They share takeaways from maturing vuln management across heterogeneous operational technology and software stacks.

talks.title: 0x10: joohoi & STÖK - Flipping Bits: Your Credentials Are Certainly Mine
talks.teaser: Examines 0x10: joohoi & STÖK - Flipping Bits: Your Credentials Are Certainly Mine and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Bit Flips and Typos

joohoi and STÖK open SEC-T comparing keyboard typos to single-bit memory errors that turn “Google” into “Coogle” or “WordPress” into “GordPress.” One flipped bit in a DNS query can redirect OAuth flows to attacker-controlled domains.

Bit Squatting History

They reference Artem Dinaburg’s DEF CON research on registering one-bit-off domains to catch DNS requests corrupted by hardware faults or cosmic rays. Dinaburg’s coogleapis.com registration reportedly collected API tokens and JavaScript fetch traffic.

Infrastructure to Catch Flips

Reproducing the technique requires catch-all DNS, BIND, nginx, Flask logging, and careful TLS certificate planning—wildcard certs only cover one DNS label, making deep subdomains like auth.dev.api expensive to impersonate under HTTPS.

Operational Reality

joohoi parked the project for two years until a full disk alert revealed massive logs of accidental traffic. STÖK adds self-hosted email catch-all experiences receiving misdirected banking messages, showing real-world bit-flip or typo traffic is not purely theoretical.

talks.title: 0x10: Solomon Sonya - Harnessing the Power of Machine Learning to Enhance Malware...
talks.teaser: Provides 0x10: Solomon Sonya - Harnessing the Power of Machine Learning to Enhance Malware and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Motivation and scale

Solomon Sonya at SEC-T argues antivirus, SOC tooling, and compliance alone cannot keep pace with malware volume. He cites VirusTotal receiving over two million samples daily, with nearly two million distinct samples, and says new detection strategies must demystify how AI/ML/NLP convert artifacts into decisions.

Research gaps

His work targets four gaps: a uniform language for static, dynamic, and memory artifacts; an automated analysis pipeline producing standardized datasets; continuously updated benchmarks instead of decade-old corpora; and heterogeneous ensembles that raise detection precision without sacrificing accuracy.

ML foundations

Sonya walks through supervised versus unsupervised learning, labels, generalization, and basic model intuition using regression examples. He emphasizes that sufficiently advanced ML should not be treated as magic, and that personal research views do not represent the U.S. Air Force or DoD. The truncated session continues into classification and model families for malware-of-tomorrow detection.

talks.title: 0x10: Chris Farris - The Cloud is getting darker and more full of terrors
talks.teaser: Evaluates 0x10: Chris Farris - The Cloud is getting darker and more full of terrors and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## Overview
Chris Farris, Forward CloudSec organizer, tours major cloud breaches to separate customer misconfigurations from provider failures.

## Backup and Insider Disasters
UniSuper lost visibility into $12 billion in pension assets when a GCP beta tool timed out and deleted cloud backups; off-cloud copies saved the fund. A former Cisco engineer deleted 456 WebEx VMs five months after termination—identified by IP, not stolen credentials.

## Metadata Service Abuse
Capital One's breach exposed 100 million records via SSRF to the instance metadata service. Google mitigated metadata proxy bypass in 2013, Azure in 2017—Farris notes AWS lagged despite years of warnings.

## Takeaways
Cloud security requires immutable off-platform backups, rapid credential revocation, IMDSv2-style protections, and skepticism about shared responsibility marketing.
